votes.motion: Approve August 13, 2024 Work Session minutes, August 13, 2024 and September 3, 2024 Formal Meeting minutes, and August 13, 2024 Truth in Taxation Meeting minutes
votes.description: The Council approved multiple sets of meeting minutes from prior sessions including work session, formal meetings, and truth in taxation meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 32 of 2024, declaring the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples Day in Salt Lake City
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall officially declaring the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples Day in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the Capital City Revitalization Zone Participation Agreement, Project Area, and Citywide 0.5% Sales and Use Tax
votes.description: The Council voted to close the public hearing that had been held to accept comment on the proposed participation agreement, project area, and sales and use tax related to Smith Entertainment Group and the Capital City Revitalization Zone.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Item B-2 (Lead Hazard Reduction Grant) to a future Consent Agenda for action
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on the HUD Lead Hazard Reduction Grant application and referred it to a future consent agenda, where it would fund lead-based paint mitigation and related positions.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action on the Northpoint Light Industrial Zoning Text Amendment to a future Council meeting
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on a proposed ordinance creating a new Northpoint Light Industrial (M-1A) Zoning District and deferred final action to a future meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 69 of 2024 (Zoning Map Amendment at approximately 450 East 700 South)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance amending the zoning of the property at approximately 450 East 700 South from RMF-35 to RMF-30 to enable construction of two new houses.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 70 of 2024 (Driveway and Loading Area Standards Text Amendment)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance amending Title 21A of the Salt Lake City Code pertaining to driveway and loading area standards to correct identified issues and support good urban design.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 71 of 2024 (Monument Signs in Manufacturing Districts Text Amendment)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance amending section 21A.46.100 to allow additional monument signs in Manufacturing Districts based on street frontage.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 72 of 2024 (Text Amendment to Prohibit Demolition of Dwelling Units for Parking Uses)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance prohibiting the demolition of dwelling units for stand-alone parking uses and restricting parking expansion unless additional housing units are included.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action on the City-wide Text Amendment for Gas Station Standards to a future Council meeting
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on an ordinance establishing minimum distance standards for gas stations near water bodies, parks, and open space in the secondary groundwater recharge area, and deferred final action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 73 of 2024 (Budget Amendment No. 1 for Fiscal Year 2024-25), partial adoption for items I-8 and I-9
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted a partial budget amendment for FY2025 including $450,000 for governmental immunity claims and $50,000 for economic promotion related to Sugar House road construction mitigation.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the 2025-2026 HUD General Community Development Needs Annual Public Hearing
votes.description: The Council closed the annual public hearing held to gather community input on development needs that will help prioritize HUD grant funds including CDBG, ESG, HOME, and HOPWA programs.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 74 of 2024 (Zoning Map Amendment at approximately 754 South State Street), subject to the applicant executing the development agreement attached to the ordinance
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance rezoning the property at approximately 754 South State Street from D-2 to D-1 to allow redevelopment as an urban hospital, contingent on execution of a development agreement.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 75 of 2024 (Zoning Text Amendment to the D-1 Central Business District Zone adding Hospitals and Ambulance Services as Conditional Uses)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance amending Section 21A.33.050 to add Hospitals (including accessory lodging facility) and Ambulance Services (indoor and outdoor) as conditional uses in the D-1 Central Business District.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 31 of 2024, approving the final Capital City Revitalization Zone Project Area and Participation Agreement between Salt Lake City and Smith Entertainment Group, LLC, and designating Smith Entertainment Group, LLC as the project participant, with additional motions regarding Abravanel Hall preservation and Utah Museum of Contemporary Art
votes.description: The Council approved the final participation agreement and project area for the Capital City Revitalization Zone with Smith Entertainment Group, designated SEG as project participant, and committed to collaborating on preservation and renovation of Abravanel Hall and recognizing the Utah Museum of Contemporary Art.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 68 of 2024, establishing, approving, and levying a 0.5% citywide sales and use tax on eligible transactions identified in Utah Code 59-12-402.5
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance imposing a 0.5% citywide sales and use tax for 30 years in connection with the Capital City Revitalization Zone and the Smith Entertainment Group participation agreement.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Resolution 33 of 2024, updating the City's processes for collective bargaining and employee representation, with a further motion requesting an Administration briefing on collective bargaining processes
votes.description: The Council adopted a resolution updating the City's collective bargaining and employee representation processes, and requested a public briefing from the Administration clarifying related legal concepts while affirming existing MOUs remain valid.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 76 of 2024, approving a $100,000 loan for Exotic Fast Foods, LLC, from the Economic Development Loan Fund
votes.description: The Council approved a $100,000 EDLF loan to Exotic Fast Foods, LLC, a Eurasian cuisine restaurant at 55 North Redwood Road, to assist in creating six new jobs and retaining three existing jobs.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 77 of 2024, approving a $100,000 loan for City Cakes, LLC, from the Economic Development Loan Fund
votes.description: The Council approved a $100,000 EDLF loan to City Cakes SLC, LLC, a vegan and gluten-free bakery at 1860 South 300 West, to assist in creating four to six new jobs and retaining eight existing jobs.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 78 of 2024, approving a $100,000 loan for Botanika SLC, LLC, from the Economic Development Loan Fund
votes.description: The Council approved a $100,000 EDLF loan to Botanika SLC, LLC, a small-scale grocer at 353 West 200 South, to assist in creating one new job and retaining one existing job.

votes.motion: Approve the consent agenda (setting public hearing dates for International Center fence height amendment and Mosquito Abatement District property tax report; board appointments of Seth Brown to Cultural Core Finance Committee, Polina Konuchkova to Library Board, and McCall Christensen to Planning Commission)
votes.description: The Council approved the consent agenda including setting future public hearing dates and approving three board appointments to the Cultural Core Finance Committee, Library Board, and Planning Commission.
